overall_assessment: The probabilistic calibration harness and dataset provenance architecture in Track 17 provide sound methodological guarantees. Expected Calibration Error (ECE) and Brier score implementations include necessary zero-division protections and equal-width binning guarantees. The SYNERGY passport in integration/passports/synergy-screening-benchmark.json establishes clear provenance distinguishing the local mirror fork from canonical upstream and respects the CC0-1.0 license without asserting premature generalizability claims. Methodological claims remain properly bounded to fixture-proven verification.

findings.description: Expected Calibration Error uses fixed equal-width binning; adaptive equal-frequency binning would provide enhanced stability in sparse prediction tails.
findings.recommendation: Provide adaptive quantile binning as an optional configuration for highly skewed screening probability distributions.

findings.description: Brier score calculation evaluates overall squared probability error but does not decompose into reliability, resolution, and uncertainty components.
findings.recommendation: Add Murphy decomposition for deep diagnostic inspection of active-learning ranker calibration.

findings.description: Dataset provenance enforcement via check_dataset_provenance.py successfully prevents unreviewed benchmark executions and ensures all public statements mention simulation limitations.
findings.recommendation: Preserve strict provenance passport enforcement across all third-party datasets.

calibration_notes: Methodologists will unanimously affirm that reporting PRISMA-S, ECE, and WSS without claiming unverified clinical effectiveness reflects the highest methodological integrity.
